Deep Learning Models for Stock Market Forecasting: A Comprehensive Comparative Analysis

This study presents a comprehensive comparative analysis of deep learning models for stock market forecasting using data from two prominent stock exchanges, the National Stock Exchange (NSE) and the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE).
COMPANY RNN LSTM CNN MLP MARUTI 5.63 6.33 4.30 4.71
Table 2 displays the Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) incurred in forecasting NSE values for MARUTI, HCL, and AXIS BANK using the ARIMA model over 400 days.

Similar to the training phase, we extracted day-wise closing prices for each stock, normalized the data, and applied a de -normalization process to the predicted output s, following the procedures used in the training dataset.
Table 3 illustrates the Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) derived from the neural network for a 400 -day prediction period.
The analysis focuses on extracting the daily closing prices of each stock, as investors typically base their decisions on buying or selling stocks on these prices.

The chosen training dataset is TATA MOTORS from the Auto mobile sector, covering the period from January 1, 1996, to June 30, 2015, including closing prices over 4,861 days ranging from 58.79 to 1365.15.
During the testing phase, data from the primary sectors —Automobile, Banking, and IT —were selected, corresponding to stocks including Maruti, Axis Bank, and HCL Technologies, respectively.
Only the day -wise closing prices were extracted from this dataset.
Four deep neural network architectures —MLP, RNN, LSTM, and CNN —were utilized for this analysis.
These networks underwent training using NSE data, specifically focusing on Tata Motors in the automobile sector.
A fixed window size of 200 days is employed to predict stock values for the subsequent 10 days.
The network undergoes training for 1000 epochs.
Following training, the networks were tested using data from both NSE and NYSE.
A prediction period of 400 days was considered for both ARIMA and neural network mod els to assess their performance over a specific timeframe.
To evaluate the accuracy of the predicted output, mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) was utilized and calculated using the specified formula.
